About us

The purpose of the Health and Disability Commissioner is to promote and protect the rights of consumers as set out in the Code of Health and Disability Services Consumers' Rights. This includes resolving complaints in a fair, timely, and effective way.

    HDC releases Disabled People’s | Tāngata Whaikaha Experiences of Health Services: Report on Complaints to HDC Disabled people | tāngata whaikaha are frequent users of health services, yet explicit and implicit biases toward disability in health systems remain pervasive. Disabled people continue to experience significant inequities in health outcomes, which in turn exacerbate the barriers they face to experiencing ordinary life outcomes. Gaining a better understanding of the experiences of disabled people | tāngata whaikaha in the health system, particularly when things have gone wrong, can improve our understanding of what is important to disabled people and their whānau or family. A new report HDC presents insights from complaints made to the Health and Disability Commissioner (HDC) from 2023 to 2025 about the experiences of disabled people | tāngata whaikaha when using health services. The themes in our report can help identify where health systems can better support the rights of disabled people to be upheld. HDC have made a series of recommendations in this respect. A link to the full report here: https://lnkd.in/easF8cnR

    HDC’s 'My Health Passport' is now available in an updated Easy Read format.     HDC developed 'My Health Passport' to help people share important information about themselves with health and disability services.  You can share the best way for people to communicate with you or what support you need when you are receiving their services.     You can take your 'My Health Passport' with you when you go to hospital or have appointments with other service providers, such as dentists or physiotherapists.     You can decide how much information to give under each section and may choose not to complete some sections. The information you provide is confidential and is only to help health professionals provide care that works for you.    My Health Passport is not a tool to help people diagnose or treat you. It is not a substitute for your medical records.    The updated Easy Read 'My Health Passport' can be downloaded at https://lnkd.in/gyu8jvDK   An Easy Read 'Guide for Completing My Health Passport' can be found here: https://lnkd.in/gG73wpR2

    Celebrating Te Wiki o te Reo Māori and World Patient Safety Day today. In Aotearoa New Zealand, it’s important that everyone knows their rights when it comes to health and disability care. This knowledge empowers individuals or their whānau to speak up if they have any concerns. Watch our te reo Māori video of 'Ōu Mōtika, Your Rights' which encourages everyone to be aware of their rights so they can ask questions, seek support, and ensure their voices are heard. An English version can be viewed here: https://lnkd.in/gayrzqAN
